title: Merit-based Metrics and Discount Rules
body:
Purpose
This is a working brief for GTM and Sales on how to frame unit metrics (why tokens), a shortlist of metric alternatives, tier design patterns, and operational discount rules. Goal: give sellers concise scripts and negotiable guardrails, and give product/billing a clear set of decisions to implement.

Executive summary (one paragraph)
We recommend a merit-based primary metric that directly maps to compute and customer value: tokens remain the best default for general-purpose LLM usage because they align cost with per-request compute (and are familiar to ML engineers). For customers with clearly bounded call semantics (e.g., embeddings-heavy customers or agent/call-centric integrations) provide optional metric aliases (embedding-units, API-calls, or inference-seconds) exposed as billing views and conversion rates. Tiers should be structured around predictable cost bands (Starter, Scale, Committed) and value add-ons (dedicated capacity, longer retention, prioritized support). Discount rules should be simple: volume tiers with step-down pricing, term-based committed discounts, and a firm cap on custom discounts requiring CRO approval above a threshold.

Why tokens (short and practical)
- Cost signal: Tokens correlate with GPU work and memory usage; they give predictable marginal cost behavior across model sizes, sequence lengths, and streaming behavior.
- Developer alignment: Engineering teams reason about prompt/token budgets. Tokens map to prompts, embeddings, and generated output in a way that non-technical buyers can be shown with simple examples.
- Flexibility: Token pricing composes across features (chat, complete, embed, rerank) with conversion factors, enabling a single billing surface.
- Competitive parity: Most inference-first vendors offer token-equivalent metrics; sticking to tokens reduces buyer confusion during procurement.

When tokens are not the right primary metric
- High-volume, small payload embedding workloads where API-calls or embedding-units give simpler predictability (search/semantic search products).
- Agent orchestration platforms charged per-agent-step or per-action prefer per-call or per-step metrics.
- On-device or edge inference where billing by inference-seconds or inference-ops better reflects cost.

Metric alternatives and conversion guidance (operational)
- Embedding-unit: define 1 embedding-unit = N tokens of input + descriptor (we recommend documenting the conversion table per model family).
- API-call: suitable for customers with consistent request sizes; provide a normalization factor and require usage sampling before switching.
- Inference-second / GPU-second: used for Dedicated or Private billing where wall-clock GPU time is measurable and contractually tracked.
- Seat / subscription: allowed as an overlay for SMB/PLG bundles for administrative simplicity, but must be backed by a token cap to avoid hidden cost leakage.

Tiering frameworks (patterns and recommended defaults)
- Pattern A: Usage bands + feature gating (Starter / Scale / Committed)
  - Starter: low free tier or low-commit band, pay-as-you-go token rate, self-serve onboarding, community support.
  - Scale: mid-band discounts (e.g., 10–25% off list), basic SLAs, higher rate limits, access to batch/optimize suggestions.
  - Committed: reserved capacity or committed spend with guaranteed latency SLOs, deeper discounts (25–50% depending on term), priority onboarding, named CSM.
- Pattern B: Throughput-first (for embedding/real-time workloads)
  - Measured by QPS or tokens/sec converted to a monthly committed throughput. Discounts scale with committed throughput and latency SLOs.
- Pattern C: Outcomes-forward (enterprise only)
  - Price by outcome buckets (e.g., search queries served, responses meeting quality bar) — complex, requires evals baseline and is for bespoke deals only.

Discounting language and guardrails (sales-friendly)
- Standard phrasing for offers: "We offer volume-based step discounts and optional term commitments for predictable unit pricing. Discounts are applied to token usage after crossing tier thresholds and are reviewed at renewal."
- Term (commit) discounts: 6–12 month commitments available with escalating discounts; require minimum committed ARR for dedicated capacity.
- One-time promotional credits: use for first 90 days only; cannot be converted to recurring discounts.
- Negotiation guardrail: discounts that increase gross margin impact beyond 30% over list must be escalated to Revenue Ops + CRO. Document a simple approval matrix (Sales AE up to 10% without approval; Manager 10–20%; RevOps/CRO required >20%).
- Currency of discounts: discounts apply to invoice line-items in the period they are earned; no retrospective re-pricing of past months unless explicit write-off approved.

Sales scripts and objection handling (snippets)
- Customer: "Why charge by tokens instead of API calls?"
  - Response: "Tokens map to the actual compute work and therefore the true cost driver — they let you measure and budget for prompt length, model choice, and output together. For steadier call patterns we can show an API-call view with a predictable conversion rate."
- Customer: "I have embeddings only — tokens are unpredictable."
  - Response: "For embeddings-heavy use cases we offer an embeddings billing view that converts to tokens at a fixed rate per model. We can run a usage sample on your workload to suggest the simplest billing metric."
- Customer: "We want a single per-seat price."
  - Response: "We can overlay a seat-based admin bundle that includes a token allowance and predictable overage pricing; this keeps procurement simple while retaining alignment to compute economics."

Competitive notes (short scanning memo for AE enablement)
- OpenAI/Open-source-hosted: often simple per-1000 token rates; buyers compare list rate and ask about volume discounts. Advantage: familiarity. Risk: perceived price war.
- Cloud-managed endpoints (GCP/AWS): sometimes charge by vCPU/GPU hours or by request with hidden infra multipliers. Advantage: tight cloud integration for infra teams.
- Inference vendors (specialized): may price by throughput (QPS) or commitments. Advantage: enterprise-focused SLAs.
- Positioning calls: emphasize Redwood’s unified billing surface (tokens by default) + conversion views plus clear dedicated capacity add-ons and transparent rollback policies.

Implementation notes for Product & Billing
- Expose: primary_billing_metric (string) in account settings, with mapping table to internal counters.
- Provide billing views: tokens, embedding-units, api-calls — each with a conversion rate pinned to model family and stored per-account for auditability.
- UI labels: avoid internal jargon — show simple examples (e.g., "One chat message ~ 40–500 tokens depending on length").
- Metering edge cases: streaming partial responses (charge emitted tokens only), cached responses (credit back for prefix cache hit), retries (deduplicate within short window).

Example negotiation scenarios (worked examples)
- Mid-market search app: baseline 200M embed tokens/month. Offer: switch to embedding-units at 50% of token-equivalent list rate with volume threshold at 500M; 12-month commit -> additional 20% off.
- Agent orchestration start-up: many small calls but high interaction. Offer: API-call overlay + token backstop; define a fixed conversion and a safety overage rate to avoid runaway costs.

Rollout checklist (next 90 days)
- Finalize conversion tables per model family (Applied ML).
- Implement billing-views in portal and flag for accounts (Billing).
- Create Sales one-pager, FAQ, and a short demo script showing token->call conversions (GTM enablement).
- Publish discount approval matrix in Confluence and embed Jira workflow for escalations (RevOps).

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve
- Exact discount thresholds per tier (product request: simple 3-band?)
- How to show cross-model conversion transparently without leaking performance internal metrics.
- Whether to allow historical re-pricing for deals > $1M ARR.

Appendix: quick cheat-sheet for sellers (two lines each)
- Why tokens: align to cost and prompt complexity.
- Embeddings: ask "What is your average doc length?" to estimate token-equivalent.
- Committed discount: always price vs list and show net effective price after commit.
- Ask for telemetry sample (7 days) before agreeing metric conversion for bespoke billing.

Status and next steps
This doc is a GTM draft. Please comment with objections and examples from recent deals. After consolidation we'll move this to the canonical Confluence pricing guide and produce a sales one-pager and POA for Billing implementation.
